summary: CNXC is a global CX/BPO firm whose supply chain is essentially labor + cloud/AI platforms. Earnings miss and stock crash highlight fragility in client retention and labor costs; near-term horizon is about stabilizing revenue and managing AI integration.

inputs.whyNeeded: Core service delivery for CX/BPO contracts
inputs.concentration: highly fragmented globally, but wage inflation in low-cost geographies is a risk

inputs.node: cloud/AI platforms (e.g., AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, AI APIs)
inputs.whyNeeded: Technology infrastructure for automation, analytics, and digital CX
inputs.concentration: concentrated among 3 hyperscalers, but substitutable at moderate cost
inputs.fragility: low (multiple providers, but switching costs exist)

chokepoints.why: Disruption in these regions (political, natural disaster) would spike labor costs and disrupt service delivery
If AI platform costs rise or key AI models become restricted, erodes margin on automated services

customers.why: Long-term BPO contracts generate >90% recurring revenue; client retention is key
These sectors drive demand for CX; any cyclical downturn could reduce contract volumes

geographic: US (HQ+customers), India, Philippines, Latin America (delivery centers); revenue diversified, but labor supply heavily exposed to APAC regions
substitutes: In-house CX teams (client reshoring), fully automated AI chatbots (like from Intercom/Zendesk), other BPO competitors (e.g., Teleperformance, TTEC)

bearCase: Earnings miss signals weakening client retention or pricing pressure from AI disruptors.
Labor costs in key hubs (Philippines/India) surge >10% due to wage laws or competition, crushing margins.
Large clients replace contract with fully automated AI solution, causing revenue cliff.
CNXC's technology investments fail to deliver ROI, making it a low-margin labor broker with no moat.

loadBearing.assumption: AI augments rather than replaces human agents
loadBearing.breaksIf: Major client deploys AI-only solution and cancels contract; or CNXC's own AI capabilities become commoditized
Hyperscalers raise API prices significantly or restrict access, squeezing CNXC's margins on automated services
Any macro shock or AI competition causes a 5%+ drop in retention, directly hitting revenue and margins

loadBearing.assumption: Global labor supply is accessible without disruption
loadBearing.breaksIf: Geopolitical events (e.g., Taiwan conflict, Philippines labor strikes) or new immigration laws disrupt labor flow

prediction.statement: Next quarterly earnings (FQ3 2026) will show revenue growth <3% YoY and margins declining due to wage inflation, likely causing another stock drop of >10%.
prediction.resolutionCriterion: CNXC reports FQ3 2026 revenue growth below 3% YoY or operating margin contraction >100bps vs prior-year quarter.

gaps: No detailed financials on revenue by segment or geography
No specific client names or contract concentration data
No current labor cost breakdown or wage inflation metrics
verifyThese: Verify client retention rate (>90% as assumed) from latest filings
Check if any large client announced AI-only CX replacement
Monitor wage inflation in Philippines and India via local labor indices
diminishingReturns: Stopped at hyperscaler level for cloud/AI platforms; further drilling into their GPU/HBM dependencies is not material because CNXC's exposure to those costs is indirect and aggregated, not a single-point-of-failure.
